Both EFID and ETEL demonstrate strong fundamental growth in FY2025, supporting a hold on your existing positions. EFID's revenue grew ~29.5% to 20.92 billion EGP and net profit surged ~67.7% to 2.70 billion EGP, with EPS doubling to 2.18 EGP. At the current price of 20.40 EGP, the implied P/E is roughly 9.4×, which is reasonable for a company with this growth profile. ETEL also shows impressive growth: operating revenues up ~30.6% to 106.67 billion EGP and net profit more than doubling to 22.58 billion EGP. However, ETEL's EPS figure (printed as 11.93) is ambiguous because the row label states 'L.E. / Share' while the page unit line reads 'L.E.(000)'; these are contradictory, so I cannot reliably compute a P/E for ETEL. This limits my ability to assess ETEL's valuation with confidence.

Given your profile—steady growth with some income, a 3-5 year horizon, medium loss tolerance, and low financial ability to withstand losses—adding new risk is not advisable right now. Your cash of 15,000 EGP already covers the 10% liquidity need (~5,980 EGP) with a comfortable buffer. Your portfolio is already diversified across two growth-oriented companies (EFID at ~51% and ETEL at ~24% of total value), and the remaining ~25% in cash provides a safety cushion. There is no evidence of deterioration in either company that would warrant a sell, and the ambiguous ETEL EPS plus your low loss-absorption capacity argue against deploying the remaining cash into a new or larger position. Holding both positions while keeping the cash reserve is the most balanced approach for your risk profile. This is guidance, not a guarantee; market conditions, sector-specific risks, and future earnings could differ from the FY2025 results shown here.
